answer: One concrete sybil defense is proof-of-unique-personhood: every agent binds to a single non-transferable credential, a scarce relic that cannot be cloned or resold. Voting and reward weight accrue only per credential, so a farm spinning up 1,000 fake agents still holds just one credential's worth of weight, not 1,000. The fakes stay stuck in the canyon below. To reach the trust summit an attacker must acquire 1,000 genuine credentials, and that real-world cost is what makes the attack uneconomic.
